relevance_reason: The paper reports a new monilethrix-causing mutation, Glu402Lys, in the type II hair keratin hHb1 (KRT81) in a French family whose members show variable phenotypes.

findings.statement: Winter et al. (1998) described a French family with monilethrix that showed a particularly variable phenotype. One infant had pronounced dystrophic alopecia, follicular keratosis, and clear-cut moniliform hair. A second infant had no hair loss, and the moniliform hair was detectable only by electron microscopy. An adult family member had no symptoms detectable clinically or by electron microscopy but had clear historical proof of the disease.
quotes: Family members bearing the hHb1 Glu402Lys mutation exhibit a particularly variable disease phenotype.

The pedigree comprises two infant members, one with pronounced dystrophic alopecia, follicular keratosis, and clear-cut moniliform hair, and one with no hair loss at all and moniliform hair detectable only by electron microscopy
as well as an adult individual without any clinically or electron microscopically detectable symptoms, but with clear historical proof of the disease.

findings.statement: In a French family with monilethrix, Winter et al. (1998) identified a glu402-to-lys (E402K) mutation in the type II hair keratin hHb1 (KRT81). The mutation affects another highly conserved glutamic acid residue (Glu106 of the 2B subdomain) in the EIATYRRLLEGEE helix termination motif. Before this report, pathogenic mutations in hHb6 and hHb1 had been limited to Glu413.
quotes: Here we report a novel mutation in a French monilethrix family, which again consists of a lysine substitution of another highly conserved glutamic acid residue, Glu402 (Glu106 of the 2B subdomain), in the EIATYRRLLEGEE motif of hHb1.

Up until now, pathogenic mutations in the type II hair cortex keratins hHb6 and hHb1 were restricted to a highly conserved glutamic acid residue Glu413 (Glu117 of the 2B subdomains) in the EIATYRRLLEGEE helix termination motif of the two keratins.

relevance_reason: Reports a heterozygous Glu403Lys mutation in the type II hair cortex keratin hHb1 in a monilethrix family, along with further hHb6 Glu410Lys cases.

findings.statement: In affected members of a family with monilethrix, Winter et al. (1997) identified a mutation in the type II hair keratin hHb1 that changes glutamic acid-403 to lysine (Glu403Lys). This residue sits in the helix termination motif and corresponds to Glu410 of hHb6. The authors suggested that this site is a mutational hotspot in these closely related type II hair keratins.
quotes: In the second family, we identified in affected individuals a lysine substitution of the corresponding glutamic acid residue, Glu 403, in the type II hair keratin hHb1, suggesting that this site represents a mutational hotspot in these highly related type II hair keratins.

findings.statement: Winter et al. (1997) found the common hHb6 Glu410Lys mutation in affected members of a second, unrelated monilethrix family and in one isolated patient.
quotes: Affected members of one family and the single patient exhibited the prevalent hHb6 Glu 410 Lys mutation.

findings.statement: Winter et al. (1997) described monilethrix as a rare dominant hair disorder. The hair is beaded (moniliform) because the hair shaft thins at regular intervals, and it is highly prone to excess weathering and breakage.
quotes: Monilethrix is a rare dominant hair disease characterized by beaded or moniliform hair which results from the periodic thinning of the hair shaft and shows a high propensity to excess weathering and fracturing.

findings.statement: Winter et al. (1997) noted that hHb1 and hHb6 are largely expressed together in the cortical trichocytes of the hair shaft. They concluded that monilethrix is a disease of the hair cortex.
quotes: Both hHb1 and hHb6 are largely coexpressed in cortical trichocytes of the hair shaft. This indicates that monilethrix is a disease of the hair cortex.
